item.title: Real Madrid rocked by Thibaut Courtois INJURY BLOW just hours before El Clasico showdown with Barcelona
item.description: Real Madrid v Villarreal CF - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Real Madrid have suffered a major setback ahead of their crucial Clasico showdown against Barcelona after goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois was ruled out through illness. His late withdrawal forces the club to rely on deputy Andriy Lunin for the vital Liga fixture at Camp Nou. Madrid suffer massive Courtois blow Madrid will be without key goalkeeper Courtois for their highly anticipated Clasico encounter against Barcelona. The 34-year-old has contracted the flu and will play no part in the crucial Liga fixture. His absence represents a significant setback for the visitors ahead of their trip to Camp Nou. Los Blancos currently trail league leaders Barcelona by six points in the table. This makes their matchday 10 clash a must-win game to keep pace in the title race. Club confirms late withdrawal from squad The illness struck at the worst possible time for the away side. Madrid released an official update confirming the goalkeeper's unexpected absence just hours before kick-off. "Courtois is a last-minute withdrawal from tonight's LaLiga matchday 10 game between Real Madrid and Barcelona due to a bout of the flu," the club said in a brief statement . "Illia Voloshyn has been called up to the squad in his place." Courtois had been in excellent form since the recent international break. He most recently played a starring role in Madrid's comprehensive 4-1 Champions League victory over RB Leipzig in midweek. Lunin ready to step into spotlight With Courtois sidelined, Lunin will take his place between the posts. The 27-year-old has proven himself as a reliable deputy for Madrid in recent seasons. Lunin notably stepped up during Madrid's successful run to the Champions League final in 2024. He will need to produce a similarly composed performance to keep a flawless Barcelona side at bay. The home side enter the fixture in spectacular domestic form. Barcelona have won all of their league games so far this season, placing immense pressure on the visiting defence. Madrid face pressure in crucial Clasico Madrid enter the Camp Nou under immense scrutiny. They have already suffered two Liga defeats this season, falling short against Real Betis and Atletico Madrid. The task of closing the six-point gap is further complicated by another major attacking absence. Forward Vinícius Junior remains unavailable for the visitors as he continues to serve a four-game domestic ban .

item.title: Hoeness visits Kompany in hospital, Klose: 'All of us are stubborn'
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeness participates in the panel discussion “How Soccer Remains the King of Business” at the Sport Marke Medien Congress. (is associated with: «Hoeness visits Kompany in hospital, Klose: 'All of us are stubborn'») Peter Kneffel/dpa Bayern Munich honorary president Uli Hoeness has visited coach Vincent Kompany in hospital after his collapse at the training centre, while other club coaches in Germany wished him a speedy recovery. The Bild paper said that Hoeness went to the clinic on Saturday and also had some food for Kompany with him. Hoeness told Welt am Sonntag paper that he was shocked when he heard the news. Kompany, 40, collapsed on Friday afternoon while watching training of Bayern's reserve team and taken to hospital. Kompany had previously suffered from a virus. Bayern board member for sport Max Eberl, who reportedly also visited Kompany on Saturday, has said that Kompany would remain in hospital for a few days as tests are carried out to determine what caused the collapsed. Eberl said that Kompany was expected to be out of action "for weeks" and in appeared to confirm suggestions that Kompany was overworked when he said that in the future "we'll continue to try, even more than before, to protect him from himself." Miroslav Klose, the 2014 World Cup winner now in charge at second division Nuremberg, said that this may not be easy because "all of us are stubborn. We have to make sure ourselves that we free our mind." Klose was among a number of coaches wished Kompany well and cited the demands the coaching job brings with it. Schalke coach Miron Muslic said that "our job is very demanding" with long days and said that what he called "coaching hygiene" was all important. Niko Kovac from Bayern's big rivals and opponents next weekend Borussia Dortmund said: "It is important to give him rest at this stage. He needs the time. "We all know how exhausting the coaching job is. I know that football is nice, but it should also be the most wonderful pastime in the world when it comes to health," Kovac said. Assistant Aaron Danks will be the main man in charge for the time being at Bayern, starting with Sunday's league match at Freiburg. item.title: The glaring Chelsea problem that Xabi Alonso is yet to solve after Cole Palmer sees red
item.description: Xabi Alonso was acutely aware of Chelsea ’s dire disciplinary record when he took the job in the summer. It was something he set out to change, and early signs showed he was succeeding in that pursuit. That was until his side fell apart against rivals Tottenham Hotspur , a side they have become so accustomed to beating at their home turf, on his worst night as Blues manager so far. Cole Palmer ’s red card , which was sandwiched between two Spurs goals in the final 12 minutes, felt like one that could only happen on an occasion like this. The deciding moment was a late challenge on Conor Gallagher , his studs catching his former team-mate on the ankle. A few inches further up and it would’ve been a straight red and a three-game ban. But the outcome on the match was the same due to earlier events. His first yellow - just nine minutes earlier - was the result of ‘head-loss’ rather than an inadvertance of a contact sport. After being the victim of a cynical foul by Spurs midfielder Mateus Fernandes, who with his face on the grass clawed the ball away in a desperate attempt to stop a Chelsea attack, Palmer retaliated by barging into the downed Portuguese, connecting abdomen with face. It meant Palmer joined Fernandes in receiving a stonewall yellow. Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi thought Palmer should have seen red there and then. Cole Palmer crashes into the face of Mateus Fernandes (Reuters) Alonso insists that this was a teachable moment rather than a red flag of Palmer’s character. “I need to check the action to talk with Cole but it is one to learn for the future for sure,” he said. Alonso, assisted by his older summer recruits like Jordan Henderson and Danny Welbeck , is intent to usher in a new era of maturity at Stamford Bridge. He had made undeniable progress in this regard since his arrival; prior to this weekend, his team were conceding fewer fouls and receiving fewer cautions per 90, and hadn’t seen red this term. For the second time in three seasons, Harry won the European Golden Shoe as the continent’s top goalscorer. item.title: Australia reach World Cup semis & New Zealand get back on track
item.description: Tom Trbojevic scored a hat-trick of tries for Australia against Fiji [Getty Images] Australia edged to a 36-22 victory in a pulsating match against Fiji to book their place in the Rugby League World Cup semi-finals. Having lost their previous five meetings against Australia by an aggregate score of 246-16, a stunned Brisbane crowd watched Fiji enjoy territorial advantage in the first half and take a 16-12 lead after the break. However, the momentum switched back to Kevin Walters' side in a crucial 60-second spell. Solomone Saukuru raced in to seemingly put Fiji 20-12 ahead - but when it was ruled out for obstruction, Australia immediately went up the other end and Tom Trbojevic scored to bring the teams level. Trbojevic, who looked vulnerable in defence, crossed twice more for Australia and Jacob Preston added a further try after Semi Valemei had completed his hat-trick for Fiji. "There are definitely some areas to improve on," Trbojevic told Premier Sports. "We didn't start as we wanted to and couldn't get a flow. We just needed to play our style of footy. item.title: Schalke duo suffer nasal bone fracture and lacerations after horror head clash
item.description: Schalke duo suffer nasal bone fracture and lacerations after horror head clash Schalke 04 have confirmed that Soufiane El-Faouzi suffered a nasal bone fracture and a laceration on his forehead against 1.FC Köln. Involved in the collision, Robin Gosens sustained two lacerations on his forehead, each of which was closed with several stitches. The Royal Blues announced this following thorough examinations at the Gelsenkirchen hospital on Sunday afternoon. A decision on their return would be made "at the appropriate time," the Bundesliga club stated in a declaration. In the 38th-minute of the match that ended 0-0 with 1.FC Köln , they had both jumped up for a header and collided heads. Both El-Faouzi and Gosens were bleeding heavily and had to be substituted, but they were able to leave the pitch on their own. Thankfully, both players were responsive, but they could miss Schalke's DfB-Pokal clash with Dynamo Dresden on Wednesday.

A brace from Tasos Douvikas was enough to seal the points, but the real story for Fabregas was his team's ability to maintain high energy levels despite a congested fixture list that recently included a high-profile Champions League encounter with Manchester United . "It depends. They sleep on mats at night, get up in the morning, [and] go straight to work. Their dedication is unparalleled, I would say the Japanese when it comes to development, especially at Honda.” That dedication will be crucial as Aston Martin endures a challenging first year under F1’s new regulations. item.title: Amorim eyes raid on Manchester United for £52m defender
item.description: Amorim eyes raid on Manchester United for £52m defender Ruben Amorim is keen on a reunion with Manchester United defender Leny Yoro at AC Milan. The Serie A side are weighing up a move for the 20-year-old at the end of the season, according to reports in Italy. Calciomercato claim Yoro is on the wish-list for Milan next summer, as Amorim eyes a raid on his former club. Yoro signed for Manchester United from Lille in a £52m deal in 2024, beating Real Madrid to his signature. Yoro was viewed as one of the most promising defenders in Europe at that time, but has failed to develop as hoped. He was used out-of-position at right-back during the recent draw at Leeds United, and has already worked under three different managers. Milan are considering whether a deal can be done, with Amorim earmarking the Frenchman as an option for his back-three system. item.title: Watch: MS Dhoni has a message for younger generations like GenZ and Gen Alpha
item.description: Former India captain MS Dhoni has shared an important message for Gen Z and Gen Alpha, urging young people to stay physically active and take better care of their health. Speaking at an event alongside renowned writer Javed Akhtar, Dhoni focused on how modern lifestyles, long hours of sitting and unhealthy eating habits can affect young people in the long run. The discussion began with a question about what advice they would give to younger generations, who are dealing with difficult situations and emotional challenges. While Akhtar praised the younger generation, Dhoni chose to highlight their physical well-being. Javed Akhtar said today’s young people are better than previous generations in several ways. He admitted that his generation was often caught up in its own beliefs and principles, while young people today are showing stronger moral values. Akhtar suggested that older generations should learn from the youth instead of assuming they always have the answers. Dhoni, however, said he still had some advice to offer, particularly when it came to health and everyday habits. Dhoni urges Gen Z to play sports and stay active Dhoni explained that earlier generations naturally moved around more, which helped them digest food and maintain a healthier lifestyle. Today, people can travel from home to work using services, spend most of the day sitting in an office and then return home by car. He warned that this lack of physical activity, combined with the growing popularity of fast food, could lead to health problems later in life. Dhoni also pointed out that sugary and fried foods can be especially harmful when people do not get enough exercise. — coolfunnytshirt (@coolfunnytshirt) His advice to young people was simple: make physical activity and sports part of their daily routine. Even if an inactive lifestyle does not cause immediate problems, its effects may become more noticeable after the age of 30. The former India captain’s message was a reminder that staying healthy requires consistent effort. Along with managing modern-day pressures, young people should prioritise exercise, make healthier food choices and develop habits that support their long-term well-being.

item.title: Charles Barkley throws shade at Aaron Rodgers when talking about his dating life
item.description: Photo by Matthew Huang/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images NBA legend Charles Barkley took a shot at Pittsburgh Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers’ dating life. NFL superstar Aaron Rodgers is known for his blunt takes, including about his own former partners that he has dated throughout his life. With Rodgers in the final season of his NFL career, the Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback is no longer holding back when talking about how he has been treated poorly by his ex-partners. Another notable figure who is on a retirement tour is NBA legend Charles Barkley, who has decided to leave his job as an analyst after more than two decades. Photo by Perry Knotts/Getty Images Charles Barkley reveals what Aaron Rodgers thing he won’t do During a recent appearance on Mad Dog Sports Radio , Barkley discussed a plethora of things, including that he won’t ever throw shade at his former partners. Chuck believes if he did that, it will make him similar to Rodgers, at least in this regard. “But I tell you what though, I’m not gonna bury everybody going out the door like Aaron. I’m not gonna burn every bridge and talk bad about all my exes on my way out the door like he’s doing,” Barkley said. It’s obvious that Barkley was referencing Rodgers’ recent comments about Shailene Woodley and Danica Patrick. While many have listened to Rodgers’ side of the story, there are some, like Barkley, who believe that the legendary QB is hurting his own case by taking repeated shots at his former partners. item.title: Denver Nuggets fans make their feelings clear after Nikola Jokic says booers 'are not welcome'
item.description: Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post Nikola Jokic has angered many Denver Nuggets fans with his comments after the win against the New Orleans Pelicans. Even though the Nuggets won the game, they were poor for large parts. At one stage, they were down by 23 points, and the home support was far from happy. Jokic and his teammates were booed, but they managed to turn it around in the end and won the game by six points. However, while speaking to the media afterwards, Jokic slammed the booing supporters and declared that they are no longer welcome at the Ball Arena in Denver. Denver Nuggets fans hit back at Nikola Jokic for his ‘not welcome’ comment “I think the fans that booed us, they don’t need to come anymore,” Jokic said after the game. “If they ask me, they are not welcome anymore.” That, unsurprisingly, has not gone down well, with many Nuggets supporters claiming that their boos were the reason why their side ended up winning the game. One fan reacted by saying: “This is not the correct response.” Another wrote: “Joker should thank us because the booing helped them start playing. Jamal even said it. You play like trash, you get booed.” “Soft response. Maybe look like you care about winning before criticising people who pay for your salary,” said another. Another Nuggets supporter posted: “Pretty pathetic response from the greatest nugget of all time. The fans paid; they don’t wanna see that.” “Well, when you play like that, the boos are warranted,” said another. Fans were worried all off-season that the Nuggets were not strong enough to compete, and their fears seem to be coming true. Yes, they won against the Pelicans, but that just papers over the cracks, as there are still many hurdles before Jokic and his team can be called contenders. Up next for the Nuggets is a game against the Golden State Warriors, and that will be a much more difficult test. If they don’t perform, we expect to see some boos again. item.title: Barcelona revive interest in €30m-rated Juventus defender; move dependent on Alejandro Balde – report
item.description: Barcelona revive interest in €30m-rated Juventus defender; move dependent on Alejandro Balde – report Barcelona made quite a few signings during the summer transfer window, bringing in the likes of Anthony Gordon, Karim Adeyemi, Rodri and Joao Cancelo. One other player the Catalan club were interested in but eventually did not move for was Juventus full-back Andrea Cambiaso. Now, according to Calciomercato (h/t FCB World ), Barça have renewed their interest in the versatile full-back. The Catalans are monitoring the Italy international, who could become a serious option if someone like Alejandro Balde leaves Hansi Flick’s squad. Juventus set €30 million asking price for Cambiaso The Italian giants value Cambiaso at around €30 million, with the defender under contract until June 2029. His ability to operate on either flank makes him an attractive option for Barcelona, particularly given Flick’s preference for versatile defenders comfortable in possession. Andrea Cambiaso is a fullback on Barcelona’s radar. (Photo by Chris Ricco/Getty Images) Cambiaso has endured a difficult start to the new season, suffering from an ankle problem that has limited his involvement at Juventus. Meanwhile, Barça potentially making a move for Cambiaso could depend directly on the future of out-of-favour Alejandro Balde. Roma are considering a January loan move for the Spaniard with an option to buy, while Juventus have also previously shown interest in his services. That said, there have been no formal negotiations between the two clubs so far for either full-back. Would Cambiaso be a sensible replacement for Balde? Cambiaso’s versatility is the most exciting aspect of his profile, and he could provide squad depth on both flanks. His attacking instincts and willingness to advance into forward areas, whether overlapping or inverting into midfield, would suit Barça ‘s approach. Nevertheless, spending €30 million on another full-back would be justified only if Barça managed to recoup a similar amount or more from a sale like Balde’s. Hansi Flick already has Joao Cancelo and Xavi Espart, who can play on both flanks, and should not add another name for the sake of it. Barcelona need to make a decision on the development of Alejandro Balde. (Photo by Aitor Alcalde/Getty Images) Balde’s situation is equally serious . Although the academy graduate has struggled for minutes, he remains a young player with considerable pace and attacking potential. Allowing him to leave on loan without a purchase option would be a much better option than parting ways with him permanently. Barça should therefore assess whether signing Cambiaso would genuinely improve the squad or if they would be better off trusting Balde. It remains to be seen how Cambiaso recovers from his ankle problem and whether Barcelona make a move for him in the near future.

item.title: Uli Hoeneß: Florian Wirtz would play 'much better' for Bayern than at Liverpool
item.description: Uli Hoeneß: Florian Wirtz would play 'much better' for Bayern than at Liverpool Uli Hoeneß believes Florian Wirtz would play 'much better' for Bayern Munich than he currently does at Liverpool . The Bayern honorary president made the remarks in an interview with German newspaper Welt am Sonntag. Wirtz made his name at Bayer Leverkusen before moving to Anfield, in a then-British record deal worth up to £116m. He arrived in England as a back-to-back winner of the Bundesliga 's Player of the Season award, but the 23-year-old has not hit the heights expected. Hoeneß has been keeping a close eye on the German's fortunes and his verdict is that the problem lies in how Liverpool have used him. Hoeneß contrasted Wirtz's central role at Leverkusen with his standing in the Liverpool side, suggesting he has lost the influence that made him stand out in the Bundesliga. Bayern Munich had been interested in signing Wirtz prior to his Premier League transfer, and Hoeneß is confident the environment at the Allianz Arena would suit the midfielder more. Hoeneß questions Liverpool’s use of Wirtz: “In Leverkusen, he got every ball” "Florian Wirtz would play much better for Bayern than he does at Liverpool," Hoeneß told Welt am Sonntag . "I watch a lot of his games. They haven't integrated him properly at all. In Leverkusen, he got every ball; in Liverpool, he's just one among many." Wirtz has faced scrutiny after a slow start to his second season at Liverpool, and was singled out after the 3-0 defeat to Manchester City earlier this month. However, he has shown glimpses of improvement in recent games. The Germany international has recorded goal involvements in each of his last three appearances, and opened his goal account against Villarreal in midweek. Liverpool take on Brighton in the Premier League this afternoon, with Brighton boss Fabian Hurzeler discussing Wirtz ahead of the game. He said the Seagulls must stop Wirtz's impact as a collective, highlighting his ability in one-vs-one situations.

item.description: Naomi Osaka's last Grand Slam title came at the Australian Open in February 2021 [Getty Images] Naomi Osaka says she is "not far off" the form that saw her win four Grand Slam titles, but admits she has thought about quitting and often ponders her future. Osaka now says that she would quit tennis if her three-year-old, Shai, asked her to, despite climbing back up the world rankings and once again challenging for major titles. "It's tough, sometimes I look towards my future and I often wonder how long I'm going to play," said Osaka, as she prepares to take part in the Pan Pacific Open in Tokyo. "Because if my daughter did say she didn't want me to travel as much, I'm not the type of person to ignore that." The upcoming fixture against PSV provides the perfect opportunity for Feyenoord to put the defeat against Betis behind them [IMAGO/Photo Players Images] Konterman Dismisses Concerns After Betis Defeat Konterman admitted he had expected a draw against Real Betis, but felt Feyenoord had been unfortunate not to get a result in Spain. "I did expect a draw beforehand. It was in there too, but sometimes you have those matches where as a team you just don't quite make it and things don't go your way," he said. He pointed to the penalty incident and a handball as moments that contributed to Feyenoord's frustration, adding that such disappointments are part of football. Crucially, Konterman believes the upcoming fixture against PSV provides the perfect opportunity for Feyenoord to put the defeat behind them. "No, when you look at where Feyenoord is now, this is not a setback," he explained. "The team will have realised that they let something slip and that they did not show the audacity and nerve that they normally do. And that they will show that again on Sunday against PSV." Konterman also praised the work being done behind the scenes at Feyenoord, highlighting the coaching partnership between Giovanni van Bronckhorst and Sipke Hulshoff. "I think it's going so damn well. The formula they came up with is so good. Sipke Hulshoff, I think, is a fantastic pitch trainer and a lovely person. Together with Gio, that's a great duo," he added. Read's partnership with winger Anis Hadj Moussa is going to be crucial against PSV [IMAGO/Box to Box Pictures] Givairo Read Compared To Denzel Dumfries The former Feyenoord player also singled out right-back Givairo Read for particular praise, comparing the youngster's potential to that of former PSV defender Denzel Dumfries. "Read is simply a potential Denzel Dumfries. A top-class player. Maybe, in terms of potential, he could even be better than Dumfries. I think Read is technically more complete," Konterman said. He also highlighted Read's partnership with winger Anis Hadj Moussa, believing their understanding on Feyenoord's right flank has become an important part of the team's attacking play. "The combination with Hadj Moussa on the right is incredibly good; those two can play so well together on that flank. If Read isn't behind him, then Hadj Moussa really is less," he explained. Feyenoord’s relatively healthier squad could prove decisive in their clash against PSV [IMAGO/NurPhoto] Why Konterman Favours Feyenoord Against PSV Despite PSV's European victory, Konterman remains unconvinced that Bosz's team have found their best form . He acknowledged his admiration for the PSV manager but believes injuries and inconsistent performances could work against the defending champions. "I'm a fan of Peter Bosz. He's a real professional. I think that PSV, despite that win in Porto, is not in a flow. Certainly not. They also have some injuries there, so for me Feyenoord are the favourites," he concluded, as quoted by PSV Inside . Feyenoord will nevertheless need to overcome a difficult recent record in Eindhoven. Their last victory at the Philips Stadion came on 19 September 2021, when they secured a commanding 4-0 win. With Feyenoord leading the Eredivisie and PSV looking to build on their Porto success, Sunday's encounter offers both sides an opportunity to make a significant statement in the title race.

item.title: Injured Real Madrid defender to travel to Barcelona to support teammates in El Clasico
item.description: Injured Real Madrid defender to travel to Barcelona to support teammates in El Clasico Real Madrid defender Raul Asencio has decided to travel to Barcelona to support his teammates ahead of Sunday’s El Clasico, despite being ruled out of the crucial meeting through injury. According to a report from AS , the centre-back does not want to miss the occasion and intends to be with the squad as Los Blancos prepare for one of their biggest fixtures of the season at Camp Nou. Asencio will be unavailable on the pitch, but his decision to make the trip shows his desire to support the team during a demanding moment in the campaign. Asencio travels to Barcelona to back Real Madrid teammates With Real Madrid preparing to face Barcelona without him, Asencio has chosen to show his support in person rather than watch the contest from a distance. The defender’s presence is intended to help rally his teammates before a match in which every contribution could matter. Raul Asencio will support his teammates in Barcelona. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) His absence is an unfortunate setback, particularly given that he had been in line to make his first appearance of the season after the most recent international break. Instead, Real Madrid must manage the defensive situation without him for the Clasico. The timing is frustrating for Asencio, who will have to watch one of the campaign’s most important matches from the sidelines. However, travelling to Barcelona gives him the chance to remain close to the group and offer support away from the pitch. Real Madrid defender targets December return While missing the Clasico, Asencio is continuing to work towards his return, with his recovery progressing well. Asencio is hoping to make his comeback in December. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) As such, the defender is seeking to shorten his recovery timeline and has set his sights on returning for Real Madrid ‘s first Copa del Rey match of the season. That fixture is expected to take place on December 16, although the date remains subject to confirmation. Asencio understands that returning within roughly three months will be difficult, but he is aiming to be available for the cup opener. His recovery will depend on how his condition develops, meaning the target should be viewed as an ambition rather than a guaranteed comeback date.

item.title: Angel Reese explains what went wrong for her in eight-point display in Game 4 loss
item.description: Photo by Paras Griffin/Getty Images The WNBA Finals are all tied up at 2-2. Angel Reese spoke after the Game 4 disappointment about what didn’t work for her. After Game 2 and Game 3 of the WNBA Finals, it looked like a foregone conclusion that Angel Reese would be the Finals MVP. Atlanta had taken a 2-1 lead with one more game on their home floor, and were one win away from taking a commanding lead in the Finals. The Valkyries had other plans, though. They bounced back from their 26-point Game 3 defeat with a 67-62 win. Gabby Williams led the way for her team with a 17-point display. More importantly, they stopped Reese from going off after two consecutive monster games. The Dream star spoke about her bad night. Angel Reese says she rushed her shots and didn’t ‘take her time’ like the last two games The Dream struggled to find their rhythm offensively, with Angel held to just eight points on 2-of-12 shooting. Rhyne Howard had a great game, but it wasn’t enough for Atlanta to get the win they needed. Reese took accountability after the game. Adjusting within a series is what leads to playoff success in basketball. This is true for the teams and the individual superstars. Change begins with recognising mistakes, and Reese was upfront about what she got wrong in Game 4. “I think I rushed a lot of my shots and I didn’t take my time and finish around the basket like I’ve been doing in the last 3 games,” Reese told media at the press conference. It happens and I’m just looking forward to the next game and I’ll just be better. The straightforward statement from Angel is another sign of her maturity as a WNBA star. It is now effectively a best-of-3 contest between the two teams for the championship. Reese has shown enough during these playoffs that fans will have complete trust in the superstar. item.title: Will Saquon Barkley play in Week 7? Injury update, start or sit advice for Eagles RB
item.description: The Philadelphia Eagles have a chance to get running back Saquon Barkley back for the Week 7 game against the Dallas Cowboys on Monday night. The Eagles have been without their star running back for each of the past two weeks after Barkley came down with a hamstring injury that forced his early exit in Week 4. This week, Barkley returned to practice and logged two limited and one full session during the week before drawing the questionable tag for Monday. Here’s what we know about Barkley’s status for Week 7. MORE: Fantasy football studs and duds for Week 7 Will Saquon Barkley play in Week 7? Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (26) looks on before the game against the Chicago Bears at Soldier Field. Credit: Patrick Gorski-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Despite the questionable tag, Barkley is expected to play in Week 7 on Monday night, according to NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport . “DeVonta Smith is out, while Saquon Barkley is questionable but expected to play,” Rapoport said on Saturday afternoon. This is not at all surprising considering Barkley’s practice participation during the week. MORE: Fantasy football running back rankings for Week 7 We would have been more skeptical if Barkley only practiced on a limited basis, but the full practice on Saturday shows he’s all but confirmed to go. Saquon Barkley start or sit advice Philadelphia Eagles running back Saquon Barkley (26) warms up before the game against the Tennessee Titans at Nissan Stadium. Credit: Steve Roberts-Imagn Images via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The Eagles are in a bad way offensively right now after losing Jalen Hurts for the season , which has an impact on the entire offense. Not only do the Eagles have to start Tanner McKee, who is a significant downgrade from Hurts as a passer, but they are also without DeVonta Smith and Dontayvion Wicks , which should make moving the football even more difficult. That, in turn, could leave Barkley with less scoring opportunities. It could also, however, force the Eagles to lean more on him on the ground and through the air. There is legitimate concern for the Eagles’ offense, but this is a juicy matchup against a Cowboys defense that has been a sieve this season. MORE: Fantasy football quarterback rankings for Week 7 The Cowboys are permitting the eighth-most fantasy points per game to backs this season, according to CBS Sports , and the most rushing yards per game. Dallas also hasn’t been able to stop a nosebleed through the air, with the Cowboys’ defense giving up the 10th-most passing yards per contest, so even McKee and what’s left of Philly’s pass-catchers could eat. This might be the best spot for Barkley to produce for the rest of the season. He’s an easy lineup decision this week, despite the issues on the Eagles’ offense. That was held in the slightly less glamorous surroundings of Blackpool town hall, where Stanley Matthews was presented with the prize by Gabriel Hanot, the visionary editor of L’Équipe who came up with the idea of crowning the world’s best player every year. A specially commissioned china plate was also handed over by the town’s mayor before the 41-year-old Matthews, who was famously teetotal, gave a short speech. “He might have had a double carrot juice that day,” says his son, Stanley Matthews Jr, who will attend this year’s awards with his sister, Jean, and her two daughters. “There was no ceremony. ‘Here’s your Ballon d’Or, well done’, sort of thing. item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. In 2026, however, it’s difficult to measure a clásico ’s standing. Is it still the sport’s biggest fixture? Continue reading...

item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. item.title: Ousmane Dembélé quietly becomes the main man after long journey to the top
item.description: The Frenchman, who has been named the best male footballer in the world by the Guardian, has benefitted from PSG’s focus on the team rather than individuals What makes a good player great, and a great player the best? This question has been occupying me since 2014, when the Guardian first asked me to contribute to its inaugural Next Generation feature . My job was to look for a France-based talent born in 1997 who could go on to have a stellar career. After a great deal of research, I narrowed it down from my shortlist of five by asking questions not about the players’ football ability, but about other attributes: resilience, adaptability, decision-making, creativity, work ethic, response to feedback and willingness to learn. Qualities we cannot see, and are harder to measure. Continue reading...
